aspect: EXAMPLE - obligatory for men, voluntary for women
description: Servicio Militar Nacional registration - alistamiento - is obligatory for all men on turning 18 and voluntary for women. Registration with SEDENA is required to obtain the Cartilla Militar.
energy_note: Compulsory if male, optional if not.

description: The draw is held on a Sunday in November. White ball: encuadramiento in the Army or Air Force with active training. Blue: assignment to the Navy. Black: exempt from active service - but not erased from military status; the man remains 'available' to the military command of his zone.
energy_note: Black is not freedom, it is availability.

description: Those drawing white or blue complete thirteen consecutive Saturday sessions, 07:00 to 13:00. SEDENA says the format is designed not to interfere significantly with study or work.

aspect: EXAMPLE - not turning up gets you the white ball
description: Historically, those who do not attend the draw automatically receive a white ball - so absence is not avoidance.
energy_note: Skip the lottery and you have already lost it.

aspect: The cartilla is an employment document
description: Completing the phases produces the released cartilla militar, valid for administrative and employment paperwork - so the man who avoids the whole thing lacks a document civilian employers ask for.
energy_note: A military paper he needs to get an office job.

aspect: It is the one hurdle here that is only about being male
description: Almost everything else in this file hits men disproportionately. The ball draw is the only item that names sex in the statute - which makes it the cleanest possible illustration of the `mexican_men` axis.
energy_note: The only one where the law itself says men.
notes: Design note: best single example of the applies_to intersection.
